posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Yes, you reshuffle a deck when you need to either draw, discard, or play a card from the top of it and there are no cards left. You don't reshuffle just because the deck has run out - you only do so when you need to do something with a card. You do not reshuffle if you are told to "reveal" a card, and if an effect tells you to reveal multiple cards and there aren't enough left (eg using Arcane Cadence when there are only two cards left), you reveal what you can and follow the instructions for as many cards as you have.
posts.raw: Yes, you reshuffle a deck when you need to either draw, discard, or play a card from the top of it and there are no cards left. You don't reshuffle just because the deck has run out - you only do so when you need to do something with a card. You [i]do not[/i] reshuffle if you are told to "reveal" a card, and if an effect tells you to reveal multiple cards and there aren't enough left (eg using Arcane Cadence when there are only two cards left), you reveal what you can and follow the instructions for as many cards as you have.

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked:
You reshuffle when you would need to draw or play a card from that deck.  "Draw" and "Play" effects force a reshuffle, but "reveal" and "search" do not.  You also don't reshuffle just because it's empty, only when you need to "draw" or "play" and there isn't anything there.

 

Edit: Right, like Ameena said, "discard" effects as well.

Edit: Right, like Ameena said, "discard" effects as well.

posts.name: JimmytheRat
posts.cooked:
I had that exact same Self-Destruct Sequence question earlier and the consensus was that despite not saying the magic words of play/draw/discard, SDS does in fact force a reshuffle of the environment deck if there's less than two cards remaining when it comes into play.  It will manage to put two cards into the countdown pile no matter what...

Unless, of course, every enviroment card is already in play, in which case shame on you!

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
If you didn't automatically reshuffle the deck, a significant percentage of games in The Block would go like this.

Round 1:  play Prison Riot, discard cards from top of deck until Char, Time-Crazed Prisoner, Imprisoned Rogue, and maybe a duplicate of one of the last two are put in play.

Round 2:  Play another Prison Riot, get the last Inmate and discard the entire Environment deck.

Round 3:  Once Inmates are dead, ignore the Environment forever.

You really are supposed to reshuffle.
